newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker onshore, interbank eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker onshore, interbank eases late.

text.p: The Thai baht was weaker onshore late on Thursday but trade was quiet as commercial demand continued to dominate the market, dealers said.

The Thai baht had moved out to 29.10/29.20 baht per dollar in the domestic market by 1100 GMT on Thursday against 29.01/29.06 in the morning. The dollar was well-bid but most parties were sidelined awaiting developments, dealers said.
"Customers still have buying interest (for dollar) but believe the 29 level is still quite high so maybe they are waiting to buy on a dip later on," said a trader at a European bank.
The market was reluctant to see the baht soften much further for fear of testing a central bank pledge to intervene in the market, traders said.
The baht was weaker in the offshore market but trade was minimal, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 29.220/29.280 per dollar offshore against 29.030/29.130 in early morning trade.
"It (the baht) is a little bit firmer. The market is very thin, (there is) no real volume," said one dealer in Singapore.
The interbank rate eased to 15-20 percent from 18-20 percent this morning but the spread was wide as the big banks were lending selectively, dealers said.
